nodes.html: Not sure whether you need an accountant or a bookkeeper? A bookkeeper typically handles your day-to-day financial records, while an accountant focuses on tax, compliance, structure and forward planning. This Australian guide explains the difference, when you may need each, and when one firm can provide both.

nodes.html: A bookkeeper handles the day-to-day recording of transactions — invoices, bills, bank reconciliation, payroll and BAS preparation. A registered BAS Agent can also lodge your BAS. Bookkeeping is about keeping accurate, up-to-date records that form the foundation for everything else. Good bookkeeping makes the accountant's job faster and cheaper.
nodes.text: A bookkeeper handles the day-to-day recording of transactions — invoices, bills, bank reconciliation, payroll and BAS preparation. A registered BAS Agent can also lodge your BAS. Bookkeeping is about keeping accurate, up-to-date records that form the foundation for everything else. Good bookkeeping makes the accountant's job faster and cheaper.

nodes.html: An accountant takes those records and lodges returns, gives structural and tax advice, manages ATO strategy, and provides forward-looking guidance like forecasting and growth advisory. A registered tax agent can lodge returns and represent you to the ATO. Accounting is about strategy, compliance and planning — building on the bookkeeper's foundation.
nodes.text: An accountant takes those records and lodges returns, gives structural and tax advice, manages ATO strategy, and provides forward-looking guidance like forecasting and growth advisory. A registered tax agent can lodge returns and represent you to the ATO. Accounting is about strategy, compliance and planning — building on the bookkeeper's foundation.

nodes.html: Most growing businesses benefit from both — and many firms offer both under one roof. A bookkeeper keeps the monthly records current; an accountant handles the annual return, structure decisions and tax planning. If your books are simple, a single accountant-bookkeeper may suffice. If you have payroll, inventory or multiple entities, separating the roles (or using a firm with dedicated bookkeepers) often works better.

nodes.q: Is a bookkeeper cheaper than an accountant?
nodes.a: Generally yes — bookkeeping rates are lower than accountant rates because the work is transactional rather than strategic. But the two are complementary, not substitutes. Most businesses need both, and many firms offer both under one roof.
nodes.aText: Generally yes — bookkeeping rates are lower than accountant rates because the work is transactional rather than strategic. But the two are complementary, not substitutes. Most businesses need both, and many firms offer both under one roof.

nodes.q: Can a bookkeeper lodge my tax return?
nodes.a: No — only a registered tax agent can charge a fee to lodge a tax return. A registered BAS Agent can lodge your BAS, but not your income tax return. If you need a return lodged, we match you with a registered tax agent.
nodes.aText: No — only a registered tax agent can charge a fee to lodge a tax return. A registered BAS Agent can lodge your BAS, but not your income tax return. If you need a return lodged, we match you with a registered tax agent.

nodes.q: Should I hire a bookkeeper or an accountant first?
nodes.a: If your records are messy or you have regular transactions to process, a bookkeeper first makes sense — clean books make the accountant's work faster and cheaper. If your records are simple and you mainly need a return lodged, an accountant may be enough. The questionnaire helps you decide.
nodes.aText: If your records are messy or you have regular transactions to process, a bookkeeper first makes sense — clean books make the accountant's work faster and cheaper. If your records are simple and you mainly need a return lodged, an accountant may be enough. The questionnaire helps you decide.

nodes.q: Can one person be both my bookkeeper and accountant?
nodes.a: Sometimes — many firms offer both services. But for larger or more complex businesses, separating the roles (or using a firm with dedicated bookkeepers and accountants) often delivers better results. Matching identifies the right setup for your situation.
nodes.aText: Sometimes — many firms offer both services. But for larger or more complex businesses, separating the roles (or using a firm with dedicated bookkeepers and accountants) often delivers better results. Matching identifies the right setup for your situation.

nodes.q: Does a bookkeeper need to be registered?
nodes.a: To charge a fee for BAS preparation and lodgement, yes — they must be a registered BAS Agent under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009. All matched bookkeepers providing BAS services in our network have verified, current TPB registration. A bookkeeper who only records transactions does not need registration.
nodes.aText: To charge a fee for BAS preparation and lodgement, yes — they must be a registered BAS Agent under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009. All matched bookkeepers providing BAS services in our network have verified, current TPB registration. A bookkeeper who only records transactions does not need registration.

nodes.q: Can my accountant also do my bookkeeping?
nodes.a: Often yes — many firms offer both bookkeeping and accounting under one roof. In the questionnaire, tell us what you already have and what you need added, and we will match you with a firm that provides both where that suits your business.
nodes.aText: Often yes — many firms offer both bookkeeping and accounting under one roof. In the questionnaire, tell us what you already have and what you need added, and we will match you with a firm that provides both where that suits your business.

nodes.q: How quickly will my matched accountant or bookkeeper contact me?
nodes.a: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your needs.

nodes.a: Yes. The matching service is free regardless of which service you need. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched firm.
